summary: @servicetitan/quick-actions preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes 727KB obfuscated payload
details: package.json declares preinstall `node setup.mjs`. setup.mjs constructs a URL against github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases, downloads the Bun runtime at install time, then invokes execFileSync on the downloaded Bun binary to run the sibling file math_init.js from the package directory. math_init.js is a ~727KB script prefixed `// @bun @bun-cjs` and structured as a rotating string-array cipher (functions such as `WV8StW` shifting an array `MmgoCP`, a multi-thousand-entry constant table `n7gIxM`, hex-named identifiers `_0x...`) with no readable strings, so its behavior is opaque to inspection without executing the deobfuscator. The advertised package is a React UI component library (main `./dist/index.js`, peer dependencies on React/mobx/@servicetitan/*) whose functionality has no relationship to fetching an alternate language runtime or executing a large opaque script at install. Fetching a non-Node runtime to execute bundled obfuscated code on `npm install` is the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern, and the mismatch between advertised purpose and preinstall behavior is consistent with a namespace/package compromise.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
